answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie each identity to a time-locked vault stake that can be slashed on proven fraud, so creating thousands of fake agents means locking real value for each one. Reputation should then accrue slowly, like sediment settling in a lagoon, rather than being granted on signup, and each agent history must form a crystal-clear, auditable trail peers can verify before trusting it. An attacker seeking influence must therefore pay, wait, and behave well across many identities, making large-scale fakery expensive and slow.
